deep.reconstruction:
This page is part 12 of a set of notes on homotopy models, apparently written around mid-1982, since the paper is the back of CRAY printouts dated June 1982. That would place it shortly before Pursuing Stacks (begun February 1983).

The page first finishes a list of axioms for what Grothendieck calls a 'strict Quillen triple' (W, C, F): weak equivalences, cofibrations, fibrations. Axiom 4 is a correction of a struck-out formulation. It reads: W is stable under base change by any fibration f in F, and under cobase change by any cofibration g in C. In modern terms this is properness, both right and left, of a closed model category. So a 'strict' Quillen triple is a proper model structure in the sense of Bousfield–Friedlander.

The NB contrasts two ways of reaching the same structure.
- In Grothendieck's approach (test categories, asphericity), W is given first and concretely, by homological criteria such as asphericity or weak equivalence detected via the nerve and homology. W is then easy to handle.
- In the Kan–Quillen approach for semi-simplicial (simplicial) sets, W is more hidden. One starts from the cofibrations C (monomorphisms) and the trivial fibrations TF. One defines the fibrations F, the Kan fibrations, as the maps with the right lifting property against a chosen generating set (TC)_0 of 'anodyne' maps, the horn inclusions. This is the Kan extension/lifting condition, and W is derived from these data.

The open question he formulates is this. For presheaves on a general test category A, take C = monomorphisms and TC = C ∩ W, where W is defined directly by the test-category criterion. Is there an a-priori set (TC)_0 whose saturation (closure under pushouts, transfinite composition and retracts, i.e. the weakly saturated class it generates) is exactly C ∩ W? And why should this hold? He proposes to look at Gabriel–Zisman's treatment of anodyne extensions (Calculus of Fractions and Homotopy Theory, 1967).

The problem served is constructing a closed model structure on presheaves over any (local) test category, with monomorphisms as cofibrations and W given by the test-category notion of weak equivalence. In Pursuing Stacks this becomes a conjecture. It was later proved by Cisinski (thesis 2002; Astérisque 308, 2006) using anodyne extensions generated by an interval object and the small object argument / accessibility.
errors: No mathematical errors. Grothendieck caught and struck out a first formulation of axiom 4 ('any cobase change ...') and replaced it with the correct two-sided properness condition: base change along F and cobase change along C.

The phrase 'via the pair (C, TF) and ... the Kan fibrations' is compressed. Strictly, in Kan–Quillen the order is C, then TF as the maps with RLP against C, then F as the maps with RLP against the horn set (TC)_0, then W. This is a sketch rather than an error.

ideas.what: Axiom requiring W to be stable under base change along fibrations and cobase change along cofibrations, as part of a 'strict Quillen triple'
ideas.modern_name: Proper (left and right proper) closed model category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bousfield–Friedlander (1978); standard in Hirschhorn and others
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in Pursuing Stacks among the model-category axioms; not certain the term 'strict' is used there

ideas.what: Contrast: in test-category theory W is primary and given by homological/asphericity criteria, whereas in Kan–Quillen W is derived from cofibrations and a generating set of anodyne maps
ideas.modern_name: Test-category approach to homotopy types vs. cofibrantly generated model structures
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983), sections on test categories and model structures

ideas.what: Question: for a general test category, is TC = C ∩ W (C = monos) the saturation of an a-priori generating set (TC)_0 of anodyne maps, and why?
ideas.modern_name: Test model structure on presheaves on a local test category; trivial cofibrations as anodyne extensions generated by a set (cofibrant generation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); proved by D.-C. Cisinski (thesis 2002, Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (conjecture on the existence of the model structure); Cisinski's Astérisque 308 credits Grothendieck

ideas.what: Suggestion to use Gabriel–Zisman's anodyne extensions as the model for (TC)_0
ideas.modern_name: Anodyne extensions / weakly saturated classes / small object argument
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel–Zisman (1967); Quillen (small object argument); Cisinski (generalized anodyne extensions from an exact cylinder)

missed.claim: Already in 1982, before Pursuing Stacks, Grothendieck states the core problem later solved by Cisinski. The problem is to identify, for an arbitrary test category, C ∩ W with the saturation of an explicit generating set of anodyne maps, and to understand why this holds. The general existence is now proved. But a direct, explicit 'horn-like' generating set for arbitrary test categories, derived from the homological description of W, is still not fully transparent: Cisinski's generating sets involve an interval plus a possibly non-explicit set obtained by accessibility arguments. The 'why' part of his question is therefore only partly answered.
missed.quote: What remains to be understood, in the context say of general test category, is the relationship between this and the direct description TC = C∩W, and why this is just the saturation of (TC)_0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It mainly documents an earlier dating (1982) of Grothendieck's test-model-structure programme. The quest for explicit generating anodyne sets for specific shape categories (cubes, dendroidal, Θ-like categories) remains active. This is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short reflective note. It defines proper model structures and poses the question of describing trivial cofibrations on test-category presheaves as anodyne saturations. This is exactly the programme known from Pursuing Stacks and solved by Cisinski. The only modest novelty is the apparent 1982 dating and the term 'strict Quillen triple' for proper model structures.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 replacement reads 'W stable by base change by any f∈F' (base change, not cobase change). The struck-out text was 'A any cobase change by f'; the second clause, 'by cobase change by any g∈C', is correct.
'In Kan's-Quillen's point of view' — the reading Kan–Quillen appears correct.
'they get to it via [-E-] the pair (C,TF) and FSTF the Kan fibrations' — 'FSTF' is probably a garbled 'F, the Kan fibrations' (or 'F ⊂ TF'-type shorthand); uncertain.
'and in why this is' should read 'and why this is'.
Text after the theorem number reads '(characterizing a strict Quillen triple)'; 'strict' is underlined in the original.
